A 23-year-old male visits the clinic with a 2-day history of right ankle pain that began the morning after
a long run. He denies any acute injury and is currently training for a marathon. On examination, motion
testing of the ankle reveals a preference for plantarflexion and adduction. Which additional physical
examination finding is most likely to be observed? Answer Choices: (A) Peroneal tendon subluxation
(B) Anterior proximal fibular head (C) Positive anterior drawer test (D) Calcaneal varus alignment (E)
Eversion stress pain (F) Eversion (G) Lateral malleolar tenderness (H) Positive Thompson test (I)
Medial subtalar tenderness (J) Inversion
 A. Anterior proximal fibular head
B. Peroneal tendon subluxation
C. Calcaneal varus alignment
D. Inversion
E. Medial subtalar tenderness
F. Eversion
G. Positive Thompson test
H. Eversion stress pain
I. Positive anterior drawer test
J. Lateral malleolar tenderness
